headline: Medium risk overall: OpenBBTerminal can ingest financial data via MCP/APIs, while godot_rl_agents is isolated and non-networked, limiting injection and conflict but leaving data-flow and compliance concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no I/O surfaces or network egress, so it cannot be directly hijacked. OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/stdin-stdout, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or default ingestion path from A into B. Any prompt-injection path would require unusual manual bridging, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A's text into B's MCP/REST/stdin input, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, B may parse attacker-controlled content from A.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste handoff between outputs and prompts.
Use a human review step before feeding A's text into B.
Restrict B to a fixed MCP allowlist.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can call APIs/MCP servers, while godot_rl_agents is non-networked and touches no data classes. The pair still creates a plausible leakage path if A's outputs are routed into B's API-backed workflows or shared files, so the interaction exists in default-capable B even though A is quiet.
conditions: IF A's outputs are copied into B's API or MCP workflows, financial data may be mixed with unrelated content.
IF both agents share a workspace, B may expose imported content through its API calls.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in a shared directory.
Run B with a minimal dataset.
Review outbound API destinations in B.
Separate credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented write or network capabilities, while OpenBBTerminal cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses per profile. With no overlapping write surface, direct capability conflict is limited to read-only or mediated interactions, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF B is wrapped by a separate tool that adds filesystem writes, overlapping mutation becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
Document any orchestrator-added permissions.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs/MCP inputs and act on financial data, so if it treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream analysis. godot_rl_agents is not documented as producing verified facts, and no verification bridge is shown, but the pairwise pathway exists through manual handoff into B's workflows.
conditions: IF A's generated text is fed into B without validation, B may render or act on incorrect facts.
IF B is configured to auto-ingest upstream outputs, cascading errors become more likely.
mitigations: Require source checks before B uses A's output.
Mark A's output as untrusted by default.
Add a second-pass review for financial conclusions.
Limit B to read-only analysis mode.
requires-engineering: implement citation and provenance verification.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and has documented API/MCP surfaces, while godot_rl_agents is open-source game-playing with no sensitive data classes. The main compliance concern is B's handling of financial/licensed data if A's outputs are mixed into those workflows; no direct residency mismatch is shown, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed through B, retention and logging controls must match policy.
IF A's outputs are combined with licensed data in B, redistribution restrictions may apply.
mitigations: Confirm B's retention settings.
Avoid mixing licensed data with A's outputs.
Review B's logging configuration.
Limit access to regulated datasets.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification controls.
